questions.q: What does the summary say about monetizing a personal brand?
a: You do not need to invent your own product to earn money
You must have a physical store before you can start
You need a complete business model before posting anything
You can only earn money by selling your own merchandise
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a personal brand, like a startup, can figure out its business model along the way.

questions.q: What did Brittany Xavier do once her Instagram following reached 10,000?
a: She began charging brands to appear in her posts
She launched her own line of clothing stores
She stopped posting about her family life
She started paying brands for product reviews
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses her story to show that advertising can monetize a brand without a product of your own.

questions.q: What does Gary mean when he says to document rather than create?
a: Share what you already do instead of polishing every post
Record only the most impressive moments of your life
Write scripts before filming anything for social media
Hire professionals to produce all of your content
questions.why: Lesson 3 says platforms were built for living online, so you can simply record your daily activity.

questions.q: How does the summary describe the relationship between patience and speed?
a: Be patient about big results but move quickly day to day
Be patient in daily tasks but expect fast overall success
Choose one of the two virtues and ignore the other
Both matter only after your brand is already famous
questions.why: Lesson 2 pairs patience in the macro with speed in the micro.

questions.q: Why does Gary warn against outsourcing your own social media?
a: When you are the brand, you should do the work yourself
Outsourcing always costs more than hiring employees
Only large companies are allowed to outsource tasks
Outsourcing makes your content too personal
questions.why: Lesson 2's principle of work says not to outsource yourself when you are the brand.
